pages.text: "A boat!" Kkiruk called. Dari went to the dock, holding a picture letter between his flippers. Tracks dotted the snow. "I'll hand over Grandma's mainland letter myself today!"
The pelican mail-boat driver unloaded a mail sack. "Dari! A letter?" Dari gripped a shell in his mouth and flattened behind Mom. "I'm too shy..."
Thinking of the driver watching made his heart thump. Dari hid behind a mail box, flippers tight around the letter. "Can't Mom give it to him?"
Mom slipped behind the box and sat beside him. "Feeling shy? That's okay. I did, too, at first. Let's try a little at a time."
She whispered, "Not all at once. One plank, one step! First, peek your head out?" Dari peeked above the box. The driver waved a wing.
"One step with me now!" Mom held his flipper. Together they stepped onto a snowy plank. Less scary than expected! Dari began to smile. "One plank, one step!"
The last step! Mom stood right beside him. "I'm here." Dari took a big breath and offered the letter. "Please send this... to Grandma." A small voice, but he said it all!
The driver tucked the letter into his mail sack. "Thank you, Dari! Grandma will be delighted." Dari lifted his shoulders proudly and slapped his tail. "I did it!"
Now he knew the steps when shy. "One, say 'I'm shy.' Two, peek my head out first! Three, go farther one step at a time!" As the boat left, Dari waved first. "Goodbye!"
Mom lifted him high. "It's okay to be shy. Little steps help!" Even with a shy heart, one step at a time had worked. One plank, one step!
